about: Reference for the gateway export paths and type mappings. Registration lives in typescript/futureagi/package.json with exactly these entries: plain import/require conditions, so ordinary consumers resolve every subpath without a custom condition. The gateway ships in candidates: the default build runs build:gateway, the files allowlist includes dist/gateway, and stage-package.cjs keeps the exports, mappings and optional React peer. Shipping is not live gateway qualification.

scripts.build: tsc --build tsconfig.json tsconfig.esm.json tsconfig.esnext.json && tsc-alias -p tsconfig.esm.json && pnpm run postbuild && pnpm run build:gateway

notes: run-all-tests.cjs runs both root and gateway Jest suites, followed by the parity node tests. Source tests do not enable a candidate surface.
The workspace and standalone pnpm locks and npm package lock are regenerated with the registered manifest. gateway-client retains its pinned private test toolchain.

react is the only peer and is optional; only ./gateway/react needs it. pack-checks.sh tests no peers, React 17, 18, 19 and an existing React 17/OpenAI 4 tree, without --legacy-peer-deps. Candidate staging keeps this peer.
typesVersions maps the gateway subpaths for moduleResolution node10; candidate staging keeps them beside the root and webhooks mappings.
ci/gateway-client.yml is installed identically under .github/workflows after applying test-only workflow policy: read-only permissions, no release or tag pushes, no persisted checkout credentials.
